title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC Ad 6 — Christ vs Adam; vitium inherent
pass_a_gloss: Sixth: why name Christ our righteousness and sanctification, yet refuse to name Adam our sin and corruption? Only Christ's righteousness justifies and only His power sanctifies—so seek all that in Him. We cannot say likewise that Adam's sin alone damns us. We are liable for many other sins; we keep tacking habits and particular bent onto the universal corruption drawn from Adam; and Adam's deed is not ours by gift or by charging as Christ's righteousness is, but by the vice it spawned and that sticks in us—which condemns not as Adam's property or outflow, but as a vice that by nature fights God's law. Those Pelagian and Socinian needles I have answered; now for his replies to ours.
pass_b_english: To the sixth: Why is Christ called our righteousness and sanctification, and Adam not called our sin and corruption? Because we are justified by no other righteousness, sanctified by no other power, than Christ's. Therefore in Him all our righteousness and sanctification is to be sought. We cannot similarly say that we are damned by no sin but Adam's. For we are guilty of many others too, and to the universal corruption which we drew from Adam we too often add many habits, or particular determinations to certain objects; and that very sin of Adam is not ours by gift, or by imputation as Christ's righteousness is, but by reason of the vice propagated from it and inherent in us, which has power to condemn us not because it is Adam's, or flowed from Adam, but because by its nature it is a vice opposed to God's law. I have answered his little questions for Pelagius and Socinus: now let us see how he answers ours.
source_text: Ad 6. Cur Christus justitia & sanctificatio nostra dicitur, Adamus non dicitur peccatum & corruptio nostra? Quia nulla alia justitia justificamur, nulla alia virtute sanctificamur, quam Christi. Itaque in eo omnis nostra justitia & sanctificatio quaerenda. Non possumus similiter dicere, nullo nos peccato damnari, quam Adami. Nam & multorum aliorum sumus rei, & ad universalem corruptionem, quam ab Adamo traximus, multos habitus, seu particulares ad certa objecta determinationes nimis saepe adjungimus, & illud ipsum Adami peccatum non est nostrum donatione, aut imputatione ut Christi justitia, sed ratione propagati ex eo vitii nobis inhaerentis, quod vim habet nos condemnandi, non quia est Adami, aut profluxit ab Adamo, sed quia natura sua vitium est legi Dei repugnans. Ejus pro Pelagio & Socino quaestiunculis respondi: nunc videamus quomodo respondeat nostris.

choices.choice: Christ unique; Adam-sin ours by inherent propagated vice not donation/imputation
